priorities.name: Electrification
priorities.summary: Moving transport, heating and machinery off fossil fuels and onto electric power.

priorities.name: Zero waste and methane reduction
priorities.goal: Slow the growth of waste by 50% by 2035.
priorities.summary: Throwing less away, and managing the methane that waste gives off as it breaks down.

priorities.name: Resilient cities and buildings
priorities.goal: Cut the energy buildings use by 25% by 2035.
priorities.summary: Buildings that use less energy, and cities that cope better with heatwaves, floods and other extremes.

priorities.name: Green industrialisation
priorities.goal: 15% of materials used are circular (reused or recycled) by 2035.
priorities.summary: Manufacturers and producers reusing and recycling materials instead of relying on new raw materials.

priorities.name: Awareness across all areas
priorities.goal: Climate-resilient farming, and climate education reaching all of society, by 2035.
priorities.summary: Helping farmers and land managers adapt, and making climate knowledge easy for everyone to find.

questions.prompt: You're the CEO of a courier company. Your fleet of diesel vans is due to be replaced. What do you do?

answers.label: Keep the old vans running
answers.explanation: Nothing gets worse, but nothing improves either, and old diesels get less efficient with age.

answers.label: Buy new diesel vans
answers.explanation: This locks in another ten or more years of burning diesel on every delivery.

answers.label: Switch to electric vans
answers.explanation: Electric vans charged from a mostly renewable grid cut the fleet's emissions to a fraction, and they're cheaper to run.

answers.label: Buy bigger diesel trucks
answers.explanation: Heavier diesel trucks burn more fuel per kilometre, and many deliveries don't fill them.

questions.prompt: You're a property manager looking after 40 older rental homes. Your maintenance budget has room for one big project. What is it?

answers.label: Fit gas heaters in every home
answers.explanation: Gas heaters burn fossil fuel all winter, and in draughty homes much of the heat escapes.

answers.label: Insulate and fit heat pumps
answers.explanation: Insulation keeps the heat in, so an efficient heat pump needs far less energy to keep tenants warm and dry.

answers.label: Pave the gardens for parking
answers.explanation: Hard surfaces send rain straight into the drains, making surface flooding worse in a downpour.

answers.label: Fix things as tenants report them
answers.explanation: The homes keep working, but they stay cold, damp and expensive to heat.

questions.prompt: You chair the council's waste committee. The landfill is filling up fast. What do you propose?

answers.label: Run a 'waste less' campaign
answers.explanation: Awareness helps a little, but without new services most food scraps still end up in landfill.

answers.label: Cut recycling to save money
answers.explanation: Everything that was being recycled now goes to landfill, and the landfill fills even faster.

answers.label: Expand the landfill
answers.explanation: More landfill means more food scraps rotting without air and giving off methane, a powerful greenhouse gas.

answers.label: Collect food scraps, capture landfill gas
answers.explanation: Food scraps become compost instead of methane, and capturing the gas from old waste stops it escaping.

questions.prompt: You own a packaging factory. A big customer wants cheaper boxes and wrapping. How do you respond?

answers.label: Use recycled material, take back packaging
answers.explanation: Recycled material needs far less energy than new, and taking packaging back keeps it in use instead of in landfill.

answers.label: Switch to cheap single-use plastic
answers.explanation: New plastic is made from oil and gas, and single-use wrapping is thrown away within days.

answers.label: Keep using the same materials
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the factory keeps relying on new raw materials.

answers.label: Bin off-cuts to speed up the line
answers.explanation: Usable material is wasted, so even more new material has to be made to replace it.

questions.prompt: You run a sheep and beef farm on steep hill country. After a wet winter, slips have scarred several paddocks. What do you do?

answers.label: Run more stock on the hills
answers.explanation: More animals mean more methane, and heavier grazing leaves the slopes even more likely to slip.

answers.label: Farm the way the family always has
answers.explanation: The farm carries on, but the slopes stay as exposed to the next big storm as they are now.

answers.label: Plant trees on slopes, join a farm climate group
answers.explanation: Trees hold the soil and take in carbon, and learning from other farmers spreads ideas that work.

answers.label: Clear the bush for more pasture
answers.explanation: Clearing bush releases the carbon it stores and removes the roots that hold the hillside together.

questions.prompt: You're a regional councillor setting the transport budget for the next ten years. What do you back?

answers.label: A new motorway
answers.explanation: New roads tend to fill with more traffic, so emissions go up.

answers.label: Electric buses and frequent routes
answers.explanation: Frequent, electric public transport gives people a clean option that's quicker than sitting in traffic.

answers.label: Keep the budget as it is
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: most trips stay in petrol and diesel vehicles.

answers.label: Cut bus services to lower rates
answers.explanation: Fewer buses push more people into cars, so more fuel is burned every day.

questions.prompt: You're a property developer planning a new subdivision of 200 homes. Where and how do you build?

answers.label: Build to the minimum standard
answers.explanation: The homes are legal, but they'll use more energy than they need to and cope poorly with extremes.

answers.label: Fill in the wetland to fit more homes
answers.explanation: Wetlands soak up floodwater and store carbon. Filling one in loses both.

answers.label: Build on cheap land on the river flats
answers.explanation: Homes on the flood plain put families in harm's way, and repairing them after every flood uses lots of energy and materials.

answers.label: Efficient homes on higher ground
answers.explanation: Well-insulated homes use less energy, and keeping clear of the flood plain, with rain gardens, keeps people and water apart.

questions.prompt: You're the CEO of a supermarket chain. Each store throws out tonnes of unsold food every week. What's your plan?

answers.label: Donate surplus food and compost the rest
answers.explanation: Food reaches people who need it, and what's left becomes compost instead of methane in landfill.

answers.label: Overstock so the shelves always look full
answers.explanation: Ordering more than you sell means even more food is thrown away.

answers.label: Discount food near its use-by date
answers.explanation: Some food sells, but whatever is left still goes to landfill.

answers.label: Keep sending it all to landfill
answers.explanation: Rotting food in landfill gives off methane, a greenhouse gas many times stronger than carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: You're a policy maker reviewing the school curriculum. Where does climate learning fit?

answers.label: Leave it to keen science teachers
answers.explanation: Some students learn a lot, but many leave school without the basics.

answers.label: Teach it at every level, with hazard maps
answers.explanation: Students who understand climate and local hazards make better choices at home, at work and in their communities.

answers.label: Drop it to make room for other subjects
answers.explanation: A generation leaves school without the knowledge to adapt or to cut emissions.

answers.label: Cut school gardens and recycling schemes
answers.explanation: Hands-on projects that teach students to waste less and grow food are lost.

questions.prompt: You're the CEO of a construction company about to demolish an old office block. What happens to the materials?

answers.label: Use only new steel and concrete
answers.explanation: Making new steel and cement releases a lot of carbon, so ignoring reuse adds to the footprint.

answers.label: Recycle only what's easy
answers.explanation: Some material is saved, but most of it still becomes waste.

answers.label: Salvage and reuse timber, steel and concrete
answers.explanation: Reusing materials avoids the energy and emissions of making new ones, and keeps them out of landfill.

answers.label: Send it all to landfill, it's faster
answers.explanation: Valuable materials are buried, and new ones have to be made in their place.

questions.prompt: You manage a large hospital. Its old gas boilers are failing. What replaces them?

answers.label: Patch up the old boilers
answers.explanation: The hospital stays warm for now, but it keeps burning gas, and the boilers keep breaking down.

answers.label: New gas boilers
answers.explanation: This locks in decades more of burning gas to heat the building.

answers.label: Electric heat pumps
answers.explanation: Heat pumps move heat instead of making it, using a fraction of the energy, and run on mostly renewable power.

answers.label: A coal boiler, as the fuel is cheap
answers.explanation: Coal is the most carbon-heavy fuel there is, and burning it also pollutes the air around the hospital.

questions.prompt: You're the CEO of a busy sea port. Trade is growing, and the cranes and yard trucks all run on diesel. What do you invest in?

answers.label: More diesel trucks for the growth
answers.explanation: More diesel machines means more fuel burned every shift.

answers.label: Electric cranes, trucks and shore power
answers.explanation: Electric machinery runs cleaner and quieter, and shore power lets docked ships switch their engines off.

answers.label: Let ships idle their engines at the wharf
answers.explanation: Ships burning fuel while tied up add emissions and fumes right next to the city.

answers.label: Keep the current machinery
answers.explanation: Nothing gets worse, but the port keeps running on diesel as it grows.

questions.prompt: You manage a big building site. Diesel generators power everything. What do you do for the next project?

answers.label: Leave the generators idling all day
answers.explanation: Idling generators burn diesel even when nothing needs power.

answers.label: Hire extra diesel generators
answers.explanation: More generators means more diesel burned for the whole project.

answers.label: Use the same generators as before
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the site keeps running on diesel.

answers.label: Connect to the grid, use electric machinery
answers.explanation: Grid power and electric machinery cut fuel use, noise and fumes on site.

questions.prompt: You own a chain of cafés that goes through thousands of takeaway cups a day. What changes?

answers.label: Keep the same cups
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: thousands of cups still go in the bin every day.

answers.label: A reusable cup scheme, and compost scraps
answers.explanation: Reusable cups replace thousands of throwaway ones, and composting keeps coffee grounds out of landfill.

answers.label: Add free lids, sleeves and straws
answers.explanation: Extra single-use items mean even more rubbish for every coffee sold.

answers.label: Cheaper plastic-lined cups
answers.explanation: Plastic-lined cups can't be recycled or composted, so every one ends up in landfill.

questions.prompt: You're organising a summer festival for 20,000 people. How do you handle food and drink?

answers.label: Reusable cups and plates, food-scrap bins
answers.explanation: Washing and reusing cuts the rubbish to a fraction, and food scraps become compost instead of methane.

answers.label: Single-use everything, it's simpler
answers.explanation: Tens of thousands of plates, cups and cutlery go straight to landfill after one use.

answers.label: Put out the usual rubbish bins
answers.explanation: The site stays tidy, but everything still ends up in landfill.

answers.label: Hand out free plastic merchandise
answers.explanation: Cheap plastic giveaways are made from new oil and are mostly thrown away within weeks.

questions.prompt: You manage a large hotel. The breakfast buffet throws out bins of food every morning. What do you do?

answers.label: Make the buffet bigger to impress guests
answers.explanation: A bigger spread means even more food is thrown away.

answers.label: Smaller dishes, donate leftovers, compost
answers.explanation: Cooking to demand, donating what's left and composting scraps keeps food out of landfill.

answers.label: Wrap everything in single-use packets
answers.explanation: Individual packets add a pile of packaging to the food waste.

answers.label: Run the buffet as usual
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the same bins of food go to landfill each day.

questions.prompt: You're a city planner. Heatwaves are getting hotter and the city centre bakes in summer. What do you plan?

answers.label: Turn small parks into car parks
answers.explanation: Asphalt soaks up heat, and losing green space makes the centre even hotter and floods it faster.

answers.label: Keep the current plan
answers.explanation: The city stays as it is: just as hot next summer.

answers.label: Street trees, shade and cool roofs
answers.explanation: Trees and light-coloured roofs cool streets and buildings, so less energy is spent on air conditioning.

answers.label: Approve unshaded glass towers
answers.explanation: Unshaded glass buildings trap heat and need huge amounts of cooling.

questions.prompt: You manage a block of council flats in a street that floods. The budget allows one project. What is it?

answers.label: Raise power points and insulate
answers.explanation: Raised wiring and fittings recover quickly after a flood, and insulation cuts heating energy all year.

answers.label: Add bedrooms in the basement
answers.explanation: Basement bedrooms are the first rooms to flood, putting tenants in danger.

answers.label: Wait and fix things after the next flood
answers.explanation: Nothing changes until the water comes, and then repairs cost more.

answers.label: Replace the lawns with concrete
answers.explanation: Concrete sends rain straight into the drains, so the street floods sooner.

questions.prompt: You're a policy maker setting the stormwater budget for a growing city. What's the priority?

answers.label: Maintain the existing pipes
answers.explanation: The system keeps working, but it isn't ready for heavier rain.

answers.label: Pipe the streams underground and build on top
answers.explanation: Piped streams overflow in big storms, and the land on top floods.

answers.label: Cut drain maintenance to save money
answers.explanation: Blocked drains overflow in the first heavy rain.

answers.label: Restore streams and wetlands, add rain gardens
answers.explanation: Wetlands and rain gardens soak up stormwater and slow floods, and they store carbon too.

questions.prompt: You're the CEO of a clothing brand. Sales are slowing. What's your next move?

answers.label: Release a new range every week
answers.explanation: Fast fashion means more clothes made, worn briefly and thrown away.

answers.label: Destroy unsold stock to protect the brand
answers.explanation: Burning new clothes wastes every bit of energy and material that went into making them.

answers.label: Recycled fabrics, repairs and take-backs
answers.explanation: Recycled fibres and repair services keep clothes in use and cut the need for new materials.

answers.label: Keep the current range
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the brand keeps relying on new materials.

questions.prompt: You run an electronics store chain. Customers keep asking what to do with their old phones and laptops. What's your answer?

answers.label: Take back and refurbish old devices
answers.explanation: Refurbished devices and recovered metals mean fewer new ones have to be made.

answers.label: Point them to the council e-waste day
answers.explanation: Some devices get recycled, but most stay in drawers.

answers.label: Trade-in deals, then bin the old devices
answers.explanation: Throwing away working devices wastes their metals and the energy used to make them.

answers.label: Send returned items to landfill
answers.explanation: Returned devices often work fine. Burying them wastes valuable materials.

questions.prompt: You own a furniture factory. A new range is being designed. What's it made from?

answers.label: Cheap particle board that can't be repaired
answers.explanation: Furniture that can't be repaired is thrown out sooner and replaced with new.

answers.label: Reclaimed timber, built to be repaired
answers.explanation: Reclaimed timber needs no new trees, and repairable furniture lasts for decades.

answers.label: New imported tropical hardwood
answers.explanation: Logging tropical forests releases stored carbon, and shipping timber burns fuel.

answers.label: The same materials as last time
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the factory keeps relying on new raw materials.

questions.prompt: You own an orchard. Droughts and sudden downpours are getting more common. What do you do?

answers.label: Climate-suited trees and water storage
answers.explanation: Hardier varieties and stored water help the orchard cope with drought, and sharing results helps neighbours too.

answers.label: Plant right up to the riverbank
answers.explanation: Clearing riverbank plants lets soil wash away in downpours and leaves the trees exposed to floods.

answers.label: Keep growing the same varieties
answers.explanation: The orchard carries on, but it isn't any better prepared for the next drought.

answers.label: Pump more groundwater with diesel pumps
answers.explanation: Diesel pumps add emissions, and over-pumping drains the water everyone relies on.

questions.prompt: You're the editor of a regional news site. How do you cover climate this year?

answers.label: Cover climate only when disaster strikes
answers.explanation: Readers hear about climate, but only when it's too late to prepare.

answers.label: Regular local climate and hazard stories
answers.explanation: Clear, regular local reporting helps people understand their risks and what they can do.

answers.label: Cut the science reporter to save money
answers.explanation: Fewer people understand what's changing and how to prepare.

answers.label: Run stories doubting climate science for clicks
answers.explanation: Misleading stories delay action and leave people less prepared.

questions.prompt: You run a dairy farm. Milk prices are up and the bank will lend you more. What do you do?

answers.label: Add more cows on the same land
answers.explanation: More cows mean more methane, and more pressure on the soil and waterways.

answers.label: Drain the wetland for more pasture
answers.explanation: Drained wetlands release stored carbon and can no longer soak up floodwater.

answers.label: Work with an advisor on lower-emission farming
answers.explanation: Better feed, fenced waterways and planting cut emissions and help the farm cope with dry spells and floods.

answers.label: Keep the same herd and practices
answers.explanation: Nothing changes: the farm's emissions and risks stay the same.
